reason: Wording: downloaded the drepunggomangusa.org PDF and ran pdftotext on it. The copyright page is present (Snow Lion, Copyright 1997 Vesna A. Wallace and B. Alan Wallace, ISBN 1-55939-061-1). Chapter III, Adopting the Spirit of Awakening, verse 27 reads exactly: Just as a blind man might find a jewel amongst heaps of rubbish, so this Spirit of Awakening has somehow arisen in me. Wikiquote gives the same wording under Wallace and Wallace 1997, section 3.27. Caveat on the evidence, not the card: the PDF is a dharma-centre compilation, not a facsimile of the Snow Lion book. It adds Tibetan outline numbers such as [332.221.233], interleaves Finot's French, and carries its own running pages. On its own pagination verse 27 falls on page 36, not 35. So the evidence locator p. 35 is neither the compiler's page nor a checked Snow Lion page. The shipped source prints no page, so this does not reach the card, but no page should be added from this PDF. Attribution: Shantideva's Bodhicaryavatara, not on the misattribution list. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Shantideva 1 of 3 (month 2, verse 8.129 in the Padmakara version), not banned. In scope: a treatise, the same classing as the shipped month 2 line, not liturgy. It fits the gratitude theme as thanks for an undeserved good. The source line leads with the name, has no dash, is about 118 characters, and gives chapter and verse. Philosophy matches the earlier Shantideva card.
